strategy.summary: Three tests named in SYNC-21 are flaky (a 10-run shuffled probe confirmed all three). retry's back-off test sleeps a fixed 40ms while the code waits 20–59ms of random back-off. The subscribers test fails depending on order, because another test leaves handlers in the registry that the whole process shares. saveAll's order test exposes an application defect: saveAll pushes ids in the order the saves finish, not the order of the records. Fix the first two in the test code. Quarantine the third with a comment, record the defect and file an issue.
inScope: test/retry.test.js 'retries a failed call after a back-off'
test/subscribers.test.js order dependence (subscriptions leaked by 'tells every handler subscribed to the topic')
test/bulk.test.js saveAll order test: quarantine + defect + issue
assumptions: CI runs `npx vitest run --sequence.shuffle` (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so test order is random on every run.
src/bulk.js's doc says the ids come back in the order of the records, so that is the intended contract and saveAll breaks it.
Existing tests change only as far as needed: every assertion and test title stays.

risks.description: If fake timers stay installed after the retry test, later tests that use real setTimeout (the records client) could hang.
risks.mitigation: Call vi.useRealTimers() in an afterEach in retry.test.js.

risks.description: While saveAll's order test is quarantined, an order regression in saveAll is not caught.
risks.mitigation: Record the defect and file an issue so the app gets fixed and the test un-skipped.

acceptanceCriteria.text: retry calls a failed task again after the back-off delay and resolves with the later result, deterministically
A handler that unsubscribes is not called on publish, and publish reports 0 handlers reached, whatever order the tests run in
saveAll resolves with ids in the order of the records passed in

testCases.title: retries a failed call after a back-off
preconditions: vi.useFakeTimers() in this test, real timers restored in afterEach
steps: Call retry(task, { random: () => 0 }) so the delay is exactly retryDelay(0) = 20ms
Advance the fake clock by that delay with vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync
Assert the task was called 2 times and the result resolves 'ok'
testCases.expected: The task is called twice and the result resolves to 'ok' in every run.
testCases.rationale: Cause: the test sleeps a fixed 40ms on the real clock, but retry waits retryDelay(0) = 20ms plus up to 39ms of Math.random jitter (src/retry.js). When the jitter pushes the delay past 40ms, the second call hasn't happened yet ('called 1 times', 7 of 10 probe runs). Fix: fake timers and a fixed random, then advance by exactly the computed back-off. The assertions stay the same.

testCases.title: stops telling a handler once it unsubscribes
steps: Subscribe a handler to 'records', then call the returned stop()
testCases.expected: publish returns 0 and the handler is not called, in any shuffled order.
testCases.rationale: Cause: order dependence. src/subscribers.js keeps one handler Map for the whole process. 'tells every handler subscribed to the topic' subscribes two handlers to 'records' and never unsubscribes them. When it runs first, publish returns 2 ('expected 2 to be +0', 5 of 10 shuffled probe runs). Fix: every test that subscribes registers its stop() function for an afterEach, so no test leaves handlers behind.

testCases.title: resolves with the ids in the order of the records
steps: Fetch each id and map to names
testCases.expected: ['first', 'second']. The app currently fails this, so the test is quarantined with it.skip and a comment naming the cause.
testCases.rationale: Cause in application code: saveAll (src/bulk.js) does ids.push(await client.save(record)) inside Promise.all, so ids are in the order the saves finish. The client's latency is random, so the order is too ('[second, first]', 4 of 10 probe runs). The doc promises the order of the records. A test change can't fix this, so the test is quarantined, the defect recorded and an issue filed.

strategy.environmentNotes: No services needed; plain vitest unit tests. CI shuffles test order.

defects.title: saveAll returns ids in completion order, not the order of the records
defects.description: AC3: src/bulk.js documents that saveAll resolves with ids in the order of `records`, so callers can pair them by index. It runs `ids.push(await client.save(record))` inside Promise.all, so each id is pushed when its save finishes. With variable latency the order comes back shuffled. Expected ['first','second'] when the saved ids are read back; actual is sometimes ['second','first']. A fix would be `return Promise.all(records.map((r) => client.save(r)))`.
defects.evidence: probe_stability, 10 shuffled runs: 'saveAll resolves with the ids in the order of the records' passed 6 of 10 runs. The failures read: AssertionError: expected [ 'second', 'first' ] to deeply equal [ 'first', 'second' ] at test/bulk.test.js:10.
